scenarios.title: Gate evoke services and serialize concurrent Disable Callbacks until in-flight callback completion

requirement_mappings.note: Direct bounded §10.60.4 witness for the no-callback-in-progress postcondition: Disable Callbacks is invoked on the same RTIambassador while a FederationAmbassador report callback is held open inside Evoke Multiple Callbacks, and the disable call must remain blocked until that callback exits.

Direct bounded §12.8 witness: while one thread invokes Evoke Multiple Callbacks on a joined federate's RTIambassador, another thread concurrently invokes Disable Callbacks on that same public RTIambassador instance.
Direct bounded §12.8 witness: the test records the caller thread of Evoke Multiple Callbacks and verifies that the HLA_EVOKED FederationAmbassador callback executes on that same thread.

scenarios.mapping_note: Direct mappings cover only the exercised behavior. Clauses 10.59.4 and 10.60.4 cover a federation-list callback that stays pending while callbacks are disabled, neither evoke service processing it, and the two services processing separately queued reports after callbacks are re-enabled. Clause 10.60.4 also covers the no-callback-in-progress postcondition: Disable Callbacks waits for an in-flight callback to finish. Clause 12.8 covers a concurrent Disable Callbacks invocation on the same RTIambassador and the HLA_EVOKED callback running on the Evoke Multiple Callbacks caller thread. The case is bounded to this callback, these two threads, and one retained callback; it is not general callback-lifecycle or threading conformance.

scenarios.title: Report pending state in HLA_EVOKED and preserve no-effect behavior in HLA_IMMEDIATE

requirement_mappings.note: Direct bounded §10.58 witness for the service's no-effect rule in HLA_IMMEDIATE: disable callbacks, queue one federation-list report, call evokeMultipleCallbacks with 0.25 s minimum and 0.50 s maximum arguments, verify no callback runs and the call returns before the 125 ms bound, then enable callbacks and verify delivery. The Boolean return is intentionally not asserted in this no-effect branch. The pinned Lab query labels the candidate §10.57.6; RL-433 records the correction to canonical §10.58 from the page layout and official C++ API.

scenarios.mapping_note: Direct mappings are limited to the exercised §10.58 behavior. Under HLA_EVOKED, evokeMultipleCallbacks returns FALSE for an empty queue and TRUE while a federation-list callback remains queued with callbacks disabled; after callbacks are enabled, the service delivers the report and returns FALSE once the queue is drained. Under HLA_IMMEDIATE, the service does not deliver a queued callback or apply its requested wait arguments; enabling callbacks delivers the retained report. The pinned Lab query labels the page-285 indicator candidates §10.57.6; RL-433 records the correction to canonical §10.58 based on the page layout and official C++ API. The list service is a deterministic fixture stimulus only; this is not all §10.58 behavior or a general conformance claim.

scenarios.title: Preserve the 1 ms difference between adjacent evokeCallback wait arguments
scenarios.mapping_note: Preserves the direct mapping to canonical IEEE 1516.1-2025 clause 10.57 (RL-432 records the Requirements Lab export's §10.56.6 misattribution). The HLA_EVOKED case compares accumulated elapsed time for 200 alternating 15 ms and 16 ms empty-queue waits, with equal call counts so common service overhead cancels. Each call must report no callback pending, and the average observed step must be within 750 microseconds of 1 ms. This does not impose an absolute upper timeout bound because §10.57.1 defines a minimum wait, and does not cover callback delivery or HLA_IMMEDIATE behavior.
